title: Possible heart attack or acute chest pain
summary: Call emergency services immediately; consider chewable aspirin only when appropriate.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Chest Pain
actions: Stop activity, let the person rest in a comfortable position, and call emergency services immediately. Use speakerphone and follow the dispatcher.

For an alert adult with non-traumatic chest pain, it may be reasonable to chew and swallow aspirin 162 to 325 mg while waiting, unless allergic, actively bleeding, advised not to take it, or uncertain; ask the dispatcher if possible.
Help with the person’s own prescribed nitroglycerin according to their plan, but do not give another person’s medicine.
Monitor responsiveness and breathing. Start CPR and use an AED if breathing becomes absent or abnormal.
Atypical symptoms can include breathlessness, nausea, sweating, extreme weakness, back or jaw discomfort, especially in women, older adults, and people with diabetes.
prohibitions: Do not drive the person to hospital when emergency transport is available.
Do not wait for pain to become severe or persistent.
Do not give aspirin when allergy, active bleeding, or a clinician’s warning is known.

related.text: Related guide: Cardiac arrest: CPR and AED

emergencyCall.text: New non-traumatic chest pain, pressure, or related symptoms requires immediate emergency transport.
